PullRequest.Title: Fix nb stickyscroll not having outline if outline pane is closed
PullRequest.Body:

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed call path, 50-cell cap, all-at-once scheduling, provider IPC boundary, and sticky renderer's rejection of level-7+ entries are all explicit in repository code. Exact provider latency and the fraction of users enabling the default-off feature are uncertain, which limits severity rather than mechanism confidence.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Up to 50 text-model references and concurrent document-symbol provider calls, including one extension-host IPC request per cell/provider on a cold outline-model cache
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Each notebook attachment launches min(code-cell count, 50) cacheSymbols operations concurrently; provider work further multiplies by the number of registered document-symbol providers, and Promise.allSettled delays sticky content until the slowest request finishes
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: A burst of extension-host/CPU work immediately after notebook attachment and delayed sticky-header initialization, causing post-open contention and latency on code-heavy notebooks
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Sticky-scroll initialization only synchronously consumed the shared outline data source. Code-symbol resolution was initiated by the Outline pane only when code-cell symbols were enabled, so opening a notebook with sticky scroll enabled and the Outline pane closed did not fan out document-symbol requests.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new attachment handler awaits computeFullSymbols with CancellationToken.None before updating sticky content, and init does the same when sticky scroll is enabled. computeFullSymbols starts cacheSymbols for the first 50 code cells in parallel.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added RIGHT line 228 now calls `await notebookCellOutline.computeFullSymbols(CancellationToken.None)` on every view-model attachment; added line 212 also puts the same fan-out on sticky-scroll enablement/initialization.
Findings.Title: Avoid resolving every code cell before initializing sticky scroll
Findings.Impact: With sticky scroll enabled, opening or reusing an editor for a notebook containing dozens of code cells now starts up to 50 concurrent symbol-provider requests even when the Outline pane is closed. Sticky content waits for all requests, while the extension-host/CPU burst competes with the just-opened editor; disabling or switching notebooks cannot cancel it because CancellationToken.None is used.
Findings.Evidence: computeFullSymbols slices the code-cell collection to 50 and immediately pushes every cacheSymbols promise before Promise.allSettled. cacheSymbols creates a text-model reference and calls OutlineModelService.getOrCreate; on a cold/version-changed model, OutlineModel.create invokes every document-symbol provider, and extension providers cross mainThreadLanguageFeatures.ts to $provideDocumentSymbols. Notebook sticky rendering treats level 7+ entries as non-headers and skips them, while cached code symbols are created at level 8+, so this boundary work is not needed to render sticky markdown headers.
Findings.Recommendation: For sticky scroll, call `recomputeState()` on attachment so the synchronous markdown-header entries are rebuilt, and leave `computeFullSymbols` gated to the Outline-pane code-symbol feature. If code symbols become required later, resolve only relevant visible cells through a cancellable bounded limiter and do not await the full batch before the initial sticky update.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or reuse a notebook editor with notebook sticky scroll enabled while the Outline pane is closed
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The notebook list and webview become visible before onDidAttachViewModel fires, so symbol resolution is off the first-paint critical path. The changed handler then awaits the entire symbol batch before sticky content can initialize, and its concurrent provider work contends with immediate post-open interaction.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke registered extension document-symbol providers through `$provideDocumentSymbols` for each cold/version-changed cell text model
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to min(code cells, 50) calls per applicable extension provider on a cold batch; same-model requests coalesce, but notebook cells are distinct models and aggregate concurrency is unbounded up to the 50-cell cap
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Sticky scroll did not call computeFullSymbols; provider IPC was requested only by the Outline-pane path when code-cell symbols were enabled.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The editor is already visible, but sticky content waits for Promise.allSettled and the IPC/extension work competes with post-open responsiveness

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Acquire and retain a text model reference while each cell's outline model is produced
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to 50 concurrent model-reference acquisitions per attachment
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This model-resolution batch was not on the sticky-scroll attachment path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each acquisition precedes that cell's provider request and remains live through symbol computation; all must settle before sticky content updates

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The first 50 code cells in the attached notebook, multiplied by all document-symbol providers applicable to each cell language; effective cardinality is up to 50 cell model resolutions and up to 50 extension-host provider IPC requests per provider.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: computeFullSymbols creates every cacheSymbols promise before awaiting Promise.allSettled, so up to 50 cells resolve concurrently with no shared limiter. OutlineModelService coalesces concurrent requests only for the same text model; each cell has a distinct model, so it does not reduce this burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: OutlineModelService has an LRU cache of only 15 models, while the changed batch touches up to 50 distinct cell models. Cold notebooks invoke providers for all cells; repeated attachments/toggles can re-invoke most or all provider work because cacheSymbols does not consult its populated cellOutlineEntryCache and the outline-model LRU cannot retain the full batch. Empty symbol results are cached only while their outline model remains in that LRU.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: the changed call, 50-cell fan-out, lack of aggregate limiting, provider IPC path, and await before sticky update are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Sticky scroll defaults off, and provider cost depends on installed language extensions and notebook languages. Code-heavy notebooks with Python/Jupyter language providers are realistic, but exact latency and extension-host load are not measured.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium-severity regression: the diff adds unnecessary bounded-but-large eager provider fan-out to each sticky-scroll notebook attachment even though sticky rendering excludes level-7+ code entries.

Scenarios.Scenario: Enable, disable, and re-enable notebook sticky scroll on an already-open code-heavy notebook
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Enabling calls async init and delays the first sticky update/listener setup until all symbol requests settle. Disabling clears UI/listeners but cannot cancel the in-flight work because CancellationToken.None was passed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Request document symbols from extension providers for cold/evicted cell models
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to 50 cell/provider calls per enablement, potentially repeated after LRU eviction
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Toggling sticky scroll initialized content directly from existing synchronous outline entries without document-symbol IPC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks initial sticky-scroll content and listener installation, not the already-rendered notebook itself

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Up to the first 50 code cells on each enablement; repeated toggles repeat model acquisition and provider lookup, with only the 15-entry outline-model LRU available across runs.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each enablement independently starts up to 50 cell operations concurrently. There is no sticky-scroll-owned cancellation source or in-flight coalescing; overlapping enablements can therefore overlap bursts, although normal UI toggles are usually sequential.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm hits are possible for at most 15 retained outline models and unchanged versions. The separate cellOutlineEntryCache stores results but cacheSymbols does not use it to bypass provider calls, so it does not suppress repeat work.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: init explicitly awaits computeFullSymbols with a non-cancellable token before updateContent.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Rapid repeated toggling is less common than notebook attachment, but a single enablement on a large notebook is sufficient to trigger the full burst.
Scenarios.Verdict: Covered by the same reported eager fan-out finding rather than a duplicate finding.

Scenarios.Scenario: Scroll a notebook with sticky scroll enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Scroll events schedule computeContent after 100 ms; DOM replacement/layout occurs only if the sticky map changes. The changed getVisibleOutlineEntry implementation runs inside computeContent on this path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Visible cell count and the descendant count of the selected root outline entry. Binary search remains logarithmic in root entries and one root subtree is flattened per lookup.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Scroll scheduling behavior is unchanged by the diff; each existing event creates its own Delayer, but that pre-existing behavior is outside PR causality.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No external cache or expensive boundary is used by getVisibleOutlineEntry; it allocates a temporary flat list as before.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that the modified binary-search branch does not introduce a performance regression; exact-match handling can return earlier.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Root subtree sizes vary, but the diff neither increases the number of flat-list constructions nor changes asymptotic work in a demonstrated way.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: changed lookup logic has no proven added work or boundary on the scroll path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Recompute notebook outline state after symbol collection, including failures
Scenarios.CriticalPath: computeFullSymbols waits for all symbol promises and then synchronously rebuilds outline entries. The new try/catch still invokes recomputeState once on normal completion and once on exceptional completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Document-symbol provider requests reached transitively from cacheSymbols
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to 50 cells times applicable providers whenever a caller invokes computeFullSymbols
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same method already performed this fan-out for the gated Outline-pane caller.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: This boundary existed in computeFullSymbols before the diff; only the new sticky-scroll calls place it on new product paths

Scenarios.ScalingInput: All notebook cells for recomputeState and up to 50 code cells for symbol collection; this multiplicity already existed inside computeFullSymbols.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Promise.allSettled concurrency is unchanged within computeFullSymbols itself; the performance change comes from the new sticky-scroll callers.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Symbol/model cache behavior is unchanged in this file. The catch path is exceptional and does not add a normal-path duplicate recomputation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that the try/catch change itself does not materially alter normal performance.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exceptional synchronous failures are uncommon, and Promise.allSettled absorbs ordinary per-cell rejections.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding in notebookOutlineDataSource.ts; the actionable regression is the newly introduced caller frequency/path.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over both changed files and all diff pages. Submitted one medium-severity finding for the new up-to-50-way, non-cancellable document-symbol/model-resolution burst on sticky-scroll initialization and notebook attachment. The binary-search and error-handling changes showed no independently introduced performance regression.
